output.evidence: Version 3 (image 7) fulfills the brutalist concrete monument concept most completely: the cast-concrete wall reads as architecture with a visible panel grid and a true wall-to-floor junction, so the bottle stands on a defined ground plane with a soft contact shadow instead of hovering. The monument sits centered-low within the safety bounds, the dark glass keeps its sculptural edges under broad soft frontal light with cool diffuse ambient, and the upper-left typographic block (TOM FORD / TOBACCO VANILLE / EAU DE PARFUM plus the thin rule) is crisp, correctly scaled and cleanly kerned. Compared with version 1's flat seam-only wall and ambiguous footing, version 2's curved studio cyclorama with a central hotspot vignette, version 4's near-featureless gray gradient that loses the concrete material, and version 5's cooler speckled wall with a floating base and no floor line, version 3 offers the most convincing physical contact, the most controlled material render and the clearest monumental grid without any set artifacts.
remaining_problems: The rule under the headline block renders as a dark ink line rather than the specified thin copper line, so the copper accent survives only on the label plaque.
Grounding shadow under the base is very faint; a slightly firmer contact shadow would lock the monument to the floor plane.
Concrete panel joints stay soft and low-contrast near the frame edges, mildly weakening the architectural read of the wall.
